blockingFindings.description: Direct inspection of all five V187 views and six pose renders: the lower-front UpperLeg weight adjustment is present, but the skirt remains strongly faceted and angular across front, side and rear. In crouch, broad upper-thigh and shorts areas remain visible below the overskirt; in sit, the front lap still separates from the raised thighs and the skirt gathers behind the pelvis. The pose response and coverage remain unacceptable.

The V187 front and side views still show angular planar shading on the bodice and a small gray patch near the waist; the rear waist flap remains stiff. The surface ownership/cause of the waist patch is unverified. Bodice appearance remains unacceptable.

Direct same-camera crouch/sit comparison V186 vs V187: thresholded changed-render areas are 878 px² (crouch; 0.0837%) and 2,038 px² (sit; 0.1944%), localized to the lower-front skirt. This is changed-pixel area, not shorts area. The rendered shorts and skirt share the same ivory material, so visible shorts-only px² is not distinguishable from these captures; no substitute number is asserted. The canonical geometric surface-ray diagnostic gives unchanged shorts coverage of 402/885 per upper thigh in crouch and 401/885 in sit; front-lap union coverage is only 54/532 crouch and 23/532 sit. The lap therefore remains above/hipward of most anterior thigh samples, matching the visible exposed-thigh gaps. The weight change does not fix coverage; appearance, fit and release remain rejected/blocked.
